previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, anxiety, and probable sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted with epigastric pain and nausea following an MRCP with secretin, which triggered an acute flare of pancreatitis. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, Dilaudid for pain, and Reglan for nausea, avoiding Zofran due to allergy. Her lipase levels improved, and she gradually advanced to a soft diet without complications. MRCP findings confirmed chronic pancreatitis and possible sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, prompting GI consultation and plans for outpatient EUS. Her psychiatric medications were continued, with adjustments to fluoxetine. She remained pain-free, ambulatory, and mentally clear, and was discharged home with a low-fat diet plan, pain and nausea medications, and follow-up arranged with gastroenterology.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT & PLAN:  Ms ___ is a very pleasant ___ w/ h/o 
chronic pancreatitis thought ___ sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, 
multiple recent admissions for pancreatitis flare, s/p extensive 
prior work-up, who presents with nausea and abdominal pain 
consistent with pancreatitis flair
.
# Acute flair of chronic pancreatitis: etiology is related to 
abdominal exam from an outside provider. Her typical 
pancreatitis pain is sharp/crampy, located in the 
epigastrum/LUQ. She was admitted and made NPO, given IVF, and 
given pain control with PO and IV dilaudid. Nausea was well 
controlled with reglan. Her BISAP score was 0. Chronic 
pancreatitis thought to be ___ sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. 
However, she does still have her gallbladder so potentially that 
is playing a role. No obstructive LFT picture makes 
choledocholithiasis unlikely as the cause of this current 
presentation. She is supposed to have endoscopic U/S to inform 
decisions about SOD sphincterotomy vs CCY. She would look to be 
resolved, then diet would be advanced and she would get severe 
pain again. In the end, she required a week of being mostly NPO 
before her pancreatitis was resolving to the point where she 
could tolerate even a carbohydrate only diet. She has a rx for 
dilaudid at home and did not ask for or require a further pain 
prescription
.
# Anxiety/depression/PTSD: continued home medications: 
fluoxetine, clonezepam, imipramine, trazadone
.
# Anemia: iron studies were checked, and did not show evidence 
of iron deficiency anemia. Her hct was stable in the mid to low 
30___. Retic count was low. Further work-up for anemia to be 
pursued in the outpatient setting
.
=======================

# Anemia to be worked-up further in outpatient setting
